business.name: Redwood Plumbing and Heating
business.industry: Domestic and light commercial plumbing, heating, and boiler servicing
business.notes: Nine engineers, two office staff, an owner who still goes out on jobs two days a week, a part time bookkeeper on Thursdays, and the owner's daughter who does the social media on Saturdays. They bought Simpro eighteen months ago, ran it for six weeks, and went back to paper because the engineers would not use it on site. The owner describes the office as running on two spreadsheets and Denise.

processes.name: Turning job sheets into invoices
processes.description: Engineers fill in a carbon copy paper job sheet on site with the parts used, hours on site, and anything they noticed. They hand the top copy back to the office, usually on Friday, though two of them hold onto a fortnight's worth. Denise sorts the sheets into a pile by customer, then types each one into Xero as a draft invoice, looking up part prices in the pricing spreadsheet as she goes. If the handwriting is unclear she messages the engineer on WhatsApp and waits for a reply, which can take a day. Once the invoice is drafted she checks it against the original quote if there was one, then sends it to the customer from Xero.
processes.pain_description: Invoices go out between one and three weeks after the work, which the owner is certain is costing them cash. Denise says she loses most of Monday and Tuesday to it. Parts get missed off, they think roughly one invoice in ten is wrong, and customers argue about the ones that are late because they cannot remember the job. Twice last year they simply never invoiced a job at all and only found out at year end. Denise is due to retire in about two years and nobody else knows how the pricing spreadsheet works.
processes.baseline_metric: Xero shows the gap between job completion and invoice sent, currently averaging about 12 days
processes.data_notes: The job sheets are paper and handwritten. Prices live in a Google Sheet that Denise maintains by hand from supplier price lists that arrive as PDFs. Xero has the customer records and is up to date.

processes.name: Chasing unaccepted quotes
processes.description: After a survey the owner writes a quote, usually in the evening, in a Word template saved on the shared drive. He emails it as a PDF from Outlook. He means to follow up after a week but only does it when he remembers or when the diary looks empty. There is a tab in the jobs spreadsheet where quotes are supposed to be logged with the date sent, but it is filled in about half the time. If a customer accepts, the job gets added to the wall planner in the office and the spreadsheet, sometimes both.
processes.pain_description: The owner reckons they win about a third of quotes and thinks they would win more if anyone followed up, but he has no evidence either way because the log is incomplete. Nobody knows what the actual conversion rate is. A competitor quoted a customer two days after Redwood did and won the job, which is the example he keeps coming back to.
processes.data_notes: Quotes exist as PDFs in an Outlook sent folder and as Word files on the shared drive, named inconsistently. The spreadsheet log is around half complete and the dates in it are not reliable.

processes.name: Issuing and filing gas safety certificates
processes.description: After a landlord safety check the engineer completes a certificate on a Gas Safe app on his phone, which emails a PDF to the office inbox. Denise saves it to the shared drive under the property address, emails a copy to the landlord, and enters the expiry date in the renewals tab of the jobs spreadsheet. Each month she filters that tab for the next sixty days and calls or emails those landlords to book the next check.
processes.pain_description: The filing itself is fine. The renewals chase is the problem, because it depends on Denise remembering to run it and she missed it in August when she was on leave. Two properties went over their expiry date, the landlord found out from his letting agent, and Redwood lost the contract on eleven properties. The address format in the spreadsheet is inconsistent so the same property sometimes appears twice.
processes.baseline_metric: certificates issued a month, counted off the Gas Safe app, about 85
processes.data_notes: Certificates are PDFs, structured by the Gas Safe app but only readable as documents. Expiry dates are hand typed into a spreadsheet. Property addresses are free text and inconsistent.

processes.name: Restocking the vans
processes.description: Every couple of weeks each engineer writes what he needs on a list stuck to the van dashboard, or messages Denise on WhatsApp. She collates the requests, phones the merchant, and picks up or arranges delivery to the yard. The engineers then take what they need off the yard shelf, which nobody records.
processes.pain_description: Engineers turn up at jobs without the right part maybe twice a week, which means a second visit and an unhappy customer. Nobody knows what stock is on the yard shelf or in any van. The owner thinks they are losing money on parts that walk but has no way of proving it. Denise finds the WhatsApp messages hard to keep track of because they arrive while she is doing something else.
processes.data_notes: Nothing is recorded. Requests are verbal, on WhatsApp, or handwritten on a list in the van. Merchant invoices come into the office as paper or PDF and go to the bookkeeper.

processes.name: Renewing the business insurance
processes.description: Once a year the broker emails a renewal pack. The owner reads it, digs out the previous year's schedule from the filing cabinet, checks the turnover figure with the bookkeeper, and emails the broker back with any changes. He usually leaves it until the week it is due.
processes.pain_description: It is a stressful week and the owner puts it off, but it happens once a year and it has never actually gone wrong. He mentioned it because he was asked what admin he dislikes.
processes.data_notes: Renewal packs are PDFs in email. The previous schedule is paper in a filing cabinet. Turnover comes out of Xero.
